title: Mauna Loa Observatory: last direct sunlight of every evening of 2016 (NOAA GML) and the horizon towards the setting Sun (Copernicus DEM)

radius_enters_via.how: the horizon and the sea dip are computed on a sphere of radius 6,371 km from the Copernicus DEM (heights over the WGS84/EGM2008 geoid)

verdict_rule: Last light at the times a flat Sun at the model's height would give, or a sea horizon that never dips below the observatory's eye level.
license_note: NOAA GML baseline radiation data: public domain (US government). Copernicus DEM GLO-30: (c) DLR e.V. 2010-2014 and (c) Airbus Defence and Space GmbH 2014-2018, provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA; free licence.

sources.cite: NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory, baseline surface radiation, Mauna Loa (MLO), one-minute means, 2016
Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (ESA / Airbus), open bucket

units.t: minutes after 0 h UTC of the date (the Hawaii evening of the previous day)

inputs.origin: NOAA GML baseline radiation, Mauna Loa, one-minute means, 2016 (gml.noaa.gov/aftp/data/radiation/baseline/mlo/).
Copernicus DEM GLO-30 tiles (copied from data/dem/cache/cop/ on 2026-10-14); a .none marker means open sea.

notes: Every clear evening is kept; the featured one is chosen by a rule fixed in advance (closest to the median solar altitude among the clear sea-horizon evenings). The tiles live in raw/cop/ (copied from data/dem/cache/cop/ on 2026-10-14); a .none marker means no tile, open sea.
